title: KDELR2-KIF20A Axis Facilitates Bladder Cancer Growth and Metastasis
author: Li Meng et al.
materials: The T24, UMUC3 and SV-HUC-1 cells were obtained from the American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, Manassas, VA). Cells were cultured in DMEM (for UMUC3), 1640 (for T24) and F12K (for SV-HUC-1) mediums supplemented with fetal bovine serum (10%) and incubated in 5% CO2 at 37 °C.

Total RNA was extracted using the TRIzol reagent (Thermo, Massachusetts, USA) and reverse-transcribed as described previously [36]. The real-time PCR analysis was performed using SYBR Green mix (Thermo, Massachusetts, USA). Results were normalised to GAPDH in each sample. Gene primers were obtained from Sangon Biotech (Shanghai) and are listed:

GraphPad Prism 8.0 (GraphPad Software Inc.) was used to perform the statistical analyses. Results are presented as means ± standard error of the mean (SEM). Student’s t-test or one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to evaluate the differences in KDELR2 gene expression between different subgroups of patients. In addition, the Pearson correlation coefficient and chi-squared test were performed to assess the associations between KDELR2 expression levels and clinicopathological characteristics. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted, and the area under the curve (AUC) was calculated to analyse the diagnostic efficiency. The prognostic significance of KDELR2 to predict the OS and DFS of patients with BCa were estimated by the Kaplan–Meier method. Furthermore, the log-rank test was used to depict the OS or PFS distributions of the patients with different expression levels of KDELR2. A confidence threshold, p < 0.05, was considered statistically significant. *, p < 0.05; **, p < 0.01; ***, p < 0.001; ****, p < 0.0001.

steps.title: Culture bladder cell lines
steps.instruction: Obtain T24, UMUC3 and SV‑HUC‑1 cells from ATCC (Manassas, VA) and grow them in the appropriate media: DMEM for UMUC3, RPMI‑1640 for T24, and F12K for SV‑HUC‑1, each supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum; incubate at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Extract total RNA with TRIzol
steps.instruction: Lyse cultured cells and isolate total RNA using TRIzol reagent (Thermo, Massachusetts, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Reverse‑transcribe RNA to cDNA
steps.instruction: Convert the extracted RNA to cDNA using the reverse‑transcription method described previously [36].

steps.title: Perform qRT‑PCR with SYBR Green
steps.instruction: Set up quantitative real‑time PCR reactions using SYBR Green mix (Thermo, Massachusetts, USA). Include gene‑specific primers (ordered from Sangon Biotech, Shanghai) for GAPDH, KDELR2, KIF20A, MKI67, MMP2, MMP9, CAPG and CDK1 (sequences listed below). Run the PCR and normalize expression levels to GAPDH.

steps.title: Identify differentially expressed genes
steps.instruction: Download the three bladder cancer GEO datasets (GSE3167: 41 cancer + 19 normal; GSE52519: 3 cancer + 9 normal; GSE65635: 4 cancer + 8 normal) and use GEO2R to compare cancer versus normal samples. Select genes with log2FoldChange ≥ 1.0 (up‑regulated) or ≤ ‑1.0 (down‑regulated) and p‑value < 0.05 as significant differentially expressed genes.

steps.title: Conduct bioinformatic analyses
steps.instruction: Use the UCSC Xena browser to retrieve BLCA expression data from TCGA and assess correlations between KDELR2 and KIF20A, MMP2, MMP9, MKI67. Normalize expression values with the edgeR package. Obtain expression profiles of KIF20A, CDK1, CAPG, NOP10, PKM, IP6K2 and CRP from GEPIA. Note that TCGA‑BLCA contains 414 cancer and 19 non‑cancer samples; clinical and pathology data are also extracted. Additionally, download GSE32894 (224 patients) for survival analysis.

steps.title: Run GSEA in LinkedOmics
steps.instruction: Perform Gene Set Enrichment Analysis using the LinkInterpreter module of LinkedOmics. Set the minimum gene‑set size to 10, run 500 simulation permutations, and use a p‑value cut‑off of 0.05. Assess Gene Ontology biological processes.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Analyze all data with GraphPad Prism 8.0. Present results as mean ± SEM. Apply Student’s t‑test or one‑way ANOVA for group comparisons, Pearson correlation and chi‑squared tests for associations, ROC curves with AUC calculation for diagnostic performance, and Kaplan–Meier with log‑rank test for overall and disease‑free survival. Consider p < 0.05 statistically significant; denote significance as * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001, **** p < 0.0001.
